title: Microsoft Purview DLP: rename existing policies and rules (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing accurately separates the government-cloud roadmap target from the preview documented on Learn, and describes how historical records retain old names. The editor routes and PowerShell limitations are appropriately qualified. Add the policy reference citation supporting the explanation of DLP editing permissions.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let a DLP administrator rename an existing policy without recreating the entire policy.
claims.quote: This feature gives the ability for the DLP admin to rename the existing policy/rule without having to create the entire the rule or policy again.

claims.claim: The Create and deploy DLP policies page does not identify which clouds its rename preview reaches.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0].note; Scope
claims.claim: The DLP creation page lists Compliance administrator, Compliance data administrator, Information Protection, Information Protection Admin and Security administrator as role groups for creating and deploying policies.
claims.quote: The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of these role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: DLP Compliance Management is an applicable granular DLP role.
claims.quote: Granular Roles and Role Groups ... Here's a list of applicable roles. ... DLP Compliance Management

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: DLP editing permissions, granted through role groups, govern who can edit and rename DLP policies and rules.
claims.quote: Administrative unit admins need to be assigned to one of the same roles or role groups as administrators of unrestricted DLP policies in order to create and manage DLP policies for their administrative unit.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-policy-reference#policy-scoping to sources and cite it after the explanation that DLP editing permissions govern renaming; this page explicitly documents policy-management and editing permissions.
